maya: Quick async standup — routing/throttle check for API gateway 
maya: What I did: pushed route-policy change to staging (ref PR #4821), adjusted token-bucket to 200r/s for /v1/generate
maya: Blockers: saw brief 503 spikes during a load test, looks like a combo of cold starts + a stale circuit-breaker rule
jon: Can you paste the failing log line?
maya: Here's the minimal repro I used:
```
heyload -c 50 -p /v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" --rps 250 --duration 60
```
maya: Log excerpt: 2026-03-17T15:02:12Z gw[edge-1] ERROR backend_err 503 upstream_timeout route=generate pool=dedicated-2
sam: I can take a look. @maya can you also share the new policy snippet?
maya: Policy snippet (yaml):
```
- route: /v1/generate
  throttle:
    type: token_bucket
    rate: 200
    burst: 400
  auth: jwt
```
priya: FYI I rolled a canary with the fallback rule removed — might be related to fallback routing hitting an empty pool :/
sam: I'll pair with @jon to check routing table and pool drain metrics. ping me when you can.
jon: Looking at metrics now — 429s increased briefly then 503s; backend latency jumps align with GPU resizes at 15:01:xx
ops-bot: deploy-bot started canary deploy for maya/pr-4821 on staging (canary=10%)
maya: Thanks. If you find the pool drain, can we make the fallback to "best-effort" instead of hard-fail?
sam: SG. Also can someone approve my CR? @maya @priya — 2-line change in router.go
maya: I'll review after I finish verifying canary. Quick note: added a smoke e2e that hits /v1/generate with a 10-token prompt to exercise kv-cache.
jon: Nice. If the canary looks green in 30m I'll promote. :thumbsup: 
priya: No blockers from infra. Will watch SLOs. link to dashboard: https://app.redwood.co/dashboards/route/generate?since=15m
maya: Thanks team — will post final status here. :rocket:
